"Alliance strengthened #1 : Alliance for Feminist Movements - The goal of the Alliance for Feminist Movements is to signifcantly increase the funding and political support for women’s rights organizations in the Global South over the next decade and deepen understanding of the funding modalities that enable sustained and resilient feminist movements. Following the initial design phase of the Alliance, 2023 has seen it invest its time to deepen relationships, understanding the landscape of what is happening and taking part in existing initiatives to avoid duplication and build a broader sense of collaboration with both members and non-members. The Alliance's Streering Committee is made up of 2 national governments, 2 private foundations, 3 women's funds and 3 civil society organizations. This comes at a time when the world in which feminist movements are working faces a series of increasing crises and increased backlash from anti-rights actors across the globe. This has made the needs of feminist movements even more immediate, and existential in nature. ""Alliance strengthened #2: The Observatory on the Universality of Rights (OURs) - The importance of the OURs coalition, in existence since 2015, is even greater in the current landscape, where anti-rights work seems to become increasingly “trendy”, causing concerns for a possible depoliticization and ineffective duplication of the work. In November the OURs members gathered in Naivasha to re-energize relationships - via a process that includes holding several faultline conversations among members and publishing our manifesto. It was the first in-person convening of the whole coalition since 2019. 23 participants, both a mix of long-time OURs members and newcomers. By the end of the convening, the coalition reiterated the value and need to keep building and maintaining a trust-based working relationship, that despite the challenges posed by the anti-rights context, the OURS as a feminist collective has the will and capacity to analyze the scope of these challenges and produce new tactics, and coordination and information exchange remain key."

"Where is the money? For South Asian Activists - November 2023, AWID facilitated an inaugural convening of 11 feminists from either countries in South Asia: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka to co-create a a common vision for developing the feminist resourcing agenda in South Asia. The feminists represented the following constituencies: LBTI and queer movements, Dalit and Adivasi groups, sex workers, disability justice feminists, workers' rights groups, feminists affected by drug policies and other movements. Over four days the group built a common understanding and vision for the feminist resourcing agenda in South Asia. The is a crtiical space for feminist movements in South Asia to come together in a facilitate dmulti-lingual hybrid space to speak about resourcing and the barriers faced by movements to fundraise.It is the first - that we know of - movement led space to discuss such an important topic."
